queries.q: PTX ISA .version directive compatibility with the CUDA driver JIT compiler - what happens when a PTX module declares a .version newer than the installed driver supports
queries.excerpt: Indicates that this module must be compiled with tools that support an equal or greater version number.
queries.source: PTX ISA 11.1.1 .version; 13. Release Notes Table 62 (PTX ISA version -> CUDA release -> driver)
queries.bears_on: F7 and F2: a published ISA-to-driver mapping exists, so a PTX floor can be derived from a declared minimum rather than from whichever drivers sit in one fleet.

queries.q: PTX ISA .target directive enumerated architecture list, does it include sm_89 and sm_121
queries.excerpt: sm_80, sm_86, sm_87, sm_88, sm_89, // sm_8x target architectures ... sm_121a, sm_121f, sm_121, // sm_12x target architectures
queries.bears_on: Both compute capabilities recorded in the review's S0 ledger are valid PTX targets; neither is a transcription error.
queries.note: Returned as part of the first query's result set rather than as a separate request; recorded as its own row because it answers a separate claim.

queries.q: cuobjdump command line tool options for extracting ELF and PTX sections from CUDA binaries and fatbinaries
queries.excerpt: link to cuda driver dynamically ... cuModuleLoadDataEx(&g_cuModule, matrixMul_kernel_64_ptxdump, jitNumOptions, jitOptions, (void **)jitOptVals);
queries.source: CUDA driver-API JIT samples (cuLinkCreate, CU_JIT_INPUT_PTX, cuModuleLoadDataEx)
queries.bears_on: Supports the draft's S3.4 model - PTX emitted as text and JITted by a dlopen'ed driver. Note this query was ASKED about cuobjdump and returned driver-API JIT material instead; it is recorded as found for what it does support, and the cuobjdump question it failed to answer is the next row.

queries.q: cuobjdump --list-elf behaviour and exit status when the input host binary contains no embedded device code or fatbinary section
queries.note: MANDATORY entry (S3.B: without it, 'the docs said nothing' and 'I did not ask' are the same artifact). Two queries reached for cuobjdump's exit status on a binary with no device code and neither returned documentation of it. The review's F2 asserts it prints 'does not contain device code' and exits 255; that rests on the measurement printed in the review, NOT on NVIDIA documentation. The measurement stands; the appeal to authority does not exist.

crux.trigger_reason: S3.C's trigger is a changed CLI subcommand or flag, HTTP route, MCP tool, config key or output format. Asked of the guard rather than judged by eye: --match-crux-surface returns 0 over every added line and --match-shipped-surface returns 0 over every changed path. ONE added line did match --match-comparative: a verbatim quotation of a GitHub issue TITLE in the GT-5 evidence table, recording that the issue exists and is closed. It is not a claim this PR makes, relies on, reproduces or endorses, and B4's diff-reading surface (book/**.md, a ROOT-level *.md, printed literals and doc comments in shipped .rs) explicitly excludes docs/**.md. It is therefore not entered in comparative_claims[], which is for claims the PR makes: listing it there would demand a five-field comparator block for a measurement this project never took. The match is recorded HERE so that a matched-and-unmentioned predicate is not indistinguishable from one never run, and the ratio is not restated in this receipt because a ratio in a finding message with an empty comparative_claims is itself B4. It remains legible in the evidence file, the surface B4 excludes by design.

findings.text: PMAT-1092's acceptance criterion read '12 scripts/workflows/contracts ... 11 of 12 are ABSENT' where the review's headline and GT-1 read 21 paths with 19 absent.
findings.failure_scenario: The roadmap entry is the source of truth for what done means, so a criterion reading 11 of 12 is satisfied by fixing eleven paths and silently drops the other eight.
